AbstractText.Label: Background
AbstractText.content: Previous reports suggest that 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) might play a role in the antidepressant actions of (R,S)-ketamine. However, its role in the antidepressant actions of (R)-ketamine, which is more potent than (S)-ketamine, is unknown. This study was conducted to examine whether 5-HT depletion affects the antidepressant actions of (R)-ketamine in a chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) model.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: An inhibitor of 5-HT synthesis, para-chlorophenylalanine methyl ester hydrochloride (PCPA; 300 mg/kg, twice daily for 3 consecutive days), or vehicle was administered to control and CSDS susceptible mice. Levels of 5-HT and its metabolite 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) in mouse brain regions were measured using high-performance liquid chromatography. Furthermore, antidepressant effects of (R)-ketamine (10 mg/kg) in the vehicle- and PCPA-treated susceptible mice were assessed using tail suspension test (TST) and 1% sucrose preference test (SPT).

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: PCPA treatment caused marked reductions of 5-HT and 5-HIAA in the brain regions of control and CSDS susceptible mice. In TST, (R)-ketamine significantly attenuated the increased immobility time in the CSDS-susceptible mice with or without 5-HT depletion. In SPT (2 and 5 days after a single dose), (R)-ketamine significantly enhanced reduced sucrose consumption in the CSDS-susceptible mice with or without 5-HT depletion.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: These findings show that 5-HT depletion did not affect the antidepressant effects of (R)-ketamine in a CSDS model. Therefore, it is unlikely that 5-HT plays a major role in the antidepressant actions of (R)-ketamine.
